evidence.description: The workflow collapses the repeated session rows of each sapling into a single deficit mean and a single full mean per sapling before any statistical test, so repeated rows per independent unit never enter the test directly.
evidence.observed_value: one deficit mean and one full mean per sapling_id

source_refs.quoted_text:
def collapse_to_saplings(by_sapling):
    """Reduce repeated sessions to one deficit mean and one full mean per sapling."""
    sapling_ids = sorted(by_sapling)
    deficit_means = []
    full_means = []
    for sapling in sapling_ids:
        regimes = by_sapling[sapling]
        if sorted(regimes) != [DEFICIT, FULL]:
            raise ValueError("sapling " + sapling + " is missing an irrigation schedule")
        deficit_means.append(average(regimes[DEFICIT]))
        full_means.append(average(regimes[FULL]))
    return sapling_ids, deficit_means, full_means

evidence.description: The statistical procedure is a paired t-test applied to the sapling-level regime means, with degrees of freedom computed as n_saplings - 1, so the analysed sample size equals the number of independent units (16), not the number of session rows (64).

evidence.description: The report's stated degrees of freedom and test description are consistent with 16 independent saplings rather than 64 rows; independent recomputation from data/input.csv reproduces the reported values exactly (mean paired difference -24.00, SD 18.36, t(15) = -5.23, 95% CI [-33.78, -14.22]).
evidence.observed_value: t(15) = -5.23, p < 0.001, CI [-33.78, -14.22]; hand recomputation matches

sessions belonging to a sapling were first collapsed into one deficit mean and one
full mean for that sapling. The reported comparison is a two-sided paired t-test on
the 16 sapling-level regime means, giving exactly one analysed row per sapling.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show the issue was present by (1) tracing every path from the CSV rows to the test call: read_sessions groups readings by sapling and regime, collapse_to_saplings averages within sapling-regime, and stats.ttest_rel receives only the 16-element deficit_means and full_means lists, so no code path feeds the 64 session rows into a row-independent procedure; and (2) recomputing the statistics by hand from data/input.csv under both the sapling-level analysis and a hypothetical row-level analysis. The sapling-level computation reproduces the report exactly (mean difference -24.00, SD 18.36, SE 4.589, t(15) = -5.23, 95% CI [-33.78, -14.22]), whereas a row-level paired test would have reported df = 31 and different dispersion values, which do not appear anywhere in the report. Both attempts failed to demonstrate the issue.
